Load-bearing interface: actual settings K_u have off-diagonal q_ij g_u(i,j), arbitrary nonnegative unknown heterogeneous gains, baseline g_0=1 and product settings with q_ij g_u g_v. A product setting is actuator composition, not a sequence of two pulses. Sequential pulses separately acquire mixed derivatives. Selective mode S requires all within-label gains exactly1 and sum w=0. Activity-complete mode A instead measures all microscopic jump events without identifying their endpoints and allows internal actuation. Visible changes alone are not an all-event counter. Every used primitive/product setting needs a supplied finite exit-rate bound; thermodynamic ratios do not supply the access assumptions.

Product moments make the hidden flux norm observable: E_a(w)=w^T H w-2b_a^T w+c_a=sum nu_i q_ij[sum w_u g_u(i,j)-(e_a(j)-e_a(i))/2]^2. H is measured from product cross-label activity in S or total microscopic activity in A; b,c from ordinary visible statistics. The synthesis error bounds |nu(W_a-V_a)Qe_b|<=2Lambda^(3/2)sqrt(E_a), for signed zero-row-sum mathematical response V_a and W_a=sum w_u K_u; no signed-rate physical generator is requested. With mixed-time T_ab and C''_ab, <Qe_a,Qe_b>_nu=T_ab-C''_ab-2nu V_a Qe_b. Thus ||sym(Gammatilde)-Gamma||_op<=4k Lambda^(3/2) max_a sqrt(E_a). The T term is essential outside stationarity.

Control adequacy is acquired by a p-dimensional convex quadratic program minimizing E_a over ||w||_1<=W (zero sum in S). A PSD-inflated noisy upper certificate remains valid uniformly for data-fitted coefficients and returns inconclusive when requirements fail; nearly dependent controls and large W increase cost. For arbitrary finite monomial products of compact gain signatures Z, the best completion error is flux mass times conditional variance of the target given Z. In S the Z=1 atom contributes its full target square. This exactly characterizes this polynomial completion operation, not all possible experimental identification. Gain collisions cannot be repaired by degree. Separated scalar gain bands admit an explicit filter with D=O(g^-2 log(1/(g delta))), but coefficients grow like5^((D+1)/2) and product rates like2^(2D); polynomial accuracy cost at fixed band gap is not a joint polynomial bound in inverse gap.

Acquisition is finite, not a derivative oracle: corrected indicators require a known full-rank sensor channel, independent readout noise across times and magnitude<=kappa; repeated-time products use one indicator. Normalize a supplied common rate Rmax, choose tau=eta^2 rho^2/[10^6(p+1)k^4(1+W)^2], h=tau/(100k), beta=tau h^2/(100k), and use finite differences and O(p^2 k^2 kappa^4 beta^-2 log(pk/(zeta beta))) preparation trials. The roughly eta^-12 dependence is conservative and potentially enormous. Preparation/mixing waits, TV reproducibility bias, timing/switching, product rates and finite precision are charged. No minimum hidden-state mass or hidden size enters that stated sample bound. Approximate product flux error xi adds xi||w||_1^2 to squared certificates; unobserved internal residual adds W^2 eps_int^2 and must be bounded or measured.

A finite tested action library Q^j has acquired L^j,Gamma^j. Exact zero plus full support yields visible-history feedback closure for those actions and their convex mixtures. For approximate closure, every deployed hidden marginal must be dominated by C nu; then whole observed-path TV<=C T sqrt((k-1)sum_j tr Gamma^j), with rate/initial errors added. Coverage is supplied, not inferred from a small residual, and unprobed actions are not covered. A uniform path bound epsilon gives bounded-reward optimal-value error<=epsilon and reduced-policy regret<=2epsilon+beta; policy computation remains a separate task. Bounded pure-jump Borel kernels extend the algebra with nu-almost-everywhere closure and dominated deployments, not arbitrary diffusions or exploding rates.

The producer exact example fits degree4 coefficients of l1 norm105/2 from visible moments, giving zero synthesis residual and Gamma=(5/384)[[1,-1],[-1,1]] under nonstationary nu. The gain-collision residual is117/880; source-clock false cross-only closure is exposed by all-event access with residual1/24. The note preserves passive-equivalence/source-clock impossibility: arbitrary observed-only source clocks cannot distinguish matched passive laws. Finite examples and six floating mixed-time diagnostics do not instantiate the full noisy sampler or a laboratory control protocol. Next gates are actuator/product/event-access validation, sample-cost practicality, independent proof/priority review and deployment coverage.
